overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a stark performance divergence: first-person speculative space exploration hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomalies heavily outperform generic trivia. The top 5 videos all center on extreme exoplanet environments and existential cosmic physics, generating 800–1,055 views with high like engagement (up to 3.7% like-to-view ratios). Conversely, repeated uploads of biological/psychological factoids (e.g., octopus hearts, fake memories, earworms) suffer severe audience fatigue, averaging fewer than 60 views and near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Second-Person Extreme Planetary Survival ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet' (1,029 views, 38 likes), 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice' (972 views, 18 likes), and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate lifetime views and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Use visceral second-person immersive framing combined with lethal, scientifically grounded celestial hazards.

winning_patterns.pattern: Bizarre Astronomical Paradoxes & Superlatives at 19–21 Seconds
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,030 views, 36 likes) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) achieved top-tier traction. 19–21s durations consistently outperform sub-16s formats.
winning_patterns.action: Standardize runtime around 20–21 seconds to allow proper setup, suspense build, and a rapid scientific punchline.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repetitive Topic Re-uploads & Brain Trivia Recycling
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' was published 3 times (5, 10, and 53 views); 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' was uploaded 4 times (34, 87, and 220 views max).
weak_patterns.action: Cease duplicate topic generation immediately; enforce hard deduplication constraints before script creation.

weak_patterns.pattern: Mundane Psychology & Passive Human Biology Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) yield zero comments and negligible retention.
weak_patterns.action: Deprecate soft human psychology trivia unless tied to high-stakes survival or dark mystery narratives.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Onto a Magnetar?
next_video.opening_direction: Instant sensory shock: 'The moment you enter 1,000 kilometers of a magnetar, your journey is already over.' Show a human astronaut freefalling toward an ultra-dense spinning star with distorted magnetic lensing.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that before physical impact or heat even reaches you, the trillion-Gauss magnetic field strips electron clouds off your atoms, turning your body into an ultra-thin mist of single-file atomic polymers.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven 'What If You Fell Into...' immersive survival hook on a completely fresh, terrifying cosmic entity (magnetars/neutron stars), matching the 21s duration and midday UTC release slot of FACTVERSE's top-performing content.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do NOT use burning ice, Gliese 436b, diamond planets, 55 Cancri e, TrES-2b, or sideways glass rain.
Do NOT reference sharks, octopus hearts, cloud weight, earworms, or fake memories.
Must feature an entirely new celestial body (Magnetar / SGR 1806-20) not in the channel library.

experiment: Test whether introducing a macro-scale cosmic horror/survival narrative (Magnetar atomic dissolution) matches or exceeds the 1,000+ view exoplanet benchmark while maintaining a >3.5% like ratio and driving at least 3 comment debates.
